name: Maximum number of edges in a C_4 free subgraph of the n-cube.
comment: This is related to the famous conjecture of Erdős (see Erdős link).

304 <= a(7) <= 308 and a(8) >= 680. The lower bounds come from explicit constructions (see the Minamoto link); the upper bound is the formula below applied to a(6) = 132. - _Paweł Kwaczyński_, Aug 27 2026
reference: M. R. Emamy, K. P. Guan and I. J. Dejter, On fault tolerance in a 5-cube. Preprint.
H. Harborth and H. Nienborg, Maximum number of edges in a six-cube without four-cycles, Bulletin of the ICA 12 (1994) 55-60
link: József Balogh, Ping Hu, Bernard Lidický, and Hong Liu, Upper bounds on the size of 4- and 6-cycle-free subgraphs of the hypercube, arXiv:1201.0209 [math.CO], 2012; European J. Combin. 35 (2014), 75-85.
P. Brass, H. Harborth and H. Nienborg, On the maximum number of edges in a c4-free subgraph of qn, J. Graph Theory 19 (1995) 17-23
F. R. K. Chung, Subgraphs of a hypercube containing no small even cycles, J. Graph Theory 16 (1992) 273-286
Minamo Minamoto, New Lower Bounds for C4-Free Subgraphs of the Hypercubes Q6, Q7, and Q8: Constructions, Structure, and Computational Method, arXiv:2603.29127 [math.CO], 2026.
Manfred Scheucher and Paul Tabatabai, Python Script
formula: a(n) <= floor(2*n*a(n-1)/(n-1)) for n >= 2, since every edge of Q_n lies in exactly n-1 of the 2n subcubes isomorphic to Q_{n-1} (see Balogh et al.). - _Paweł Kwaczyński_, Aug 27 2026
example: a(2) = 3 since the 2-cube is the 4-cycle and one needs to remove a single edge to get rid of all 4-cycles.
author: _Jernej Azarija_, Jul 31 2014
